name.text: Combinations 4 - Complete Pascal's triangle (drag and drop)

questiontext.text:
In Pascal's triangle, each number is the sum of the two numbers directly above it. The number in row n, position r (counting from 0) is nCr. Drag the correct number into each box.

Part A: Complete the triangle

Row 0: 1

Row 1: 1, 1

Row 2: 1, 2, 1

Row 3: 1, 3, 3, 1

Row 4: 1, 4, 6, 4, 1

Row 5: 1, [[1]], [[2]], [[2]], [[1]], 1

Row 6: 1, [[5]], [[3]], [[4]], [[3]], [[5]], 1

Part B: Link the triangle to combinations

  1. 5C2 is in row 5, position 2, so 5C2 = [[2]]
  2. 6C3 is in row 6, position 3, so 6C3 = [[4]]
  3. 6C4 equals 6C2 by symmetry, so 6C4 = [[3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Each entry is the sum of the two entries above it. For row 5: 1+4 = 5, 4+6 = 10, 6+4 = 10, 4+1 = 5. For row 6: 1+5 = 6, 5+10 = 15, 10+10 = 20, 10+5 = 15, 5+1 = 6.

Row \(n\) lists \(_nC_0, {}_nC_1, \dots, {}_nC_n\), so \(_5C_2 = 10\) and \(_6C_3 = 20\).

The rows read the same from both ends, which shows \(_nC_r = {}_nC_{n-r}\). So \(_6C_4 = {}_6C_2 = 15\).
